title: AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_CONFIGURE_RPFILTER is deprecated (v1.12.1+) — setting it does nothing

detection.reason: read from the env NAMES of the aws-node DaemonSet's containers (the agent ships names, never values) — a variable injected through envFrom / the chart's extraEnv from a ConfigMap is not seen

quote: `AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_CONFIGURE_RPFILTER` has been deprecated, so setting this environment variable results in a no-op.
remediation: Remove AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_CONFIGURE_RPFILTER from the aws-node DaemonSet. From v1.12.1 the init container always configures the primary interface's rp_filter, so `false` no longer hands that job to you — anything that relied on ipamd leaving rp_filter alone must be checked.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get ds aws-node -o json | jq -r '.spec.template.spec.containers[] | .env[]? | select(.name == "AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_CONFIGURE_RPFILTER") | "\(.name)=\(.value)"'  # a printed line is a setting v1.12.1+ ignores

title: Nodes on nftables distributions (RHEL 8+, Ubuntu 21+) need VPC CNI v1.12.1+

detection.reason: which iptables backend a node's OS uses is not collected; its osImage names the distribution

quote: Prior to v1.12.1, the VPC CNI image only contained `iptables-legacy`. Newer distributions of RHEL (RHEL 8.x+), Ubuntu (Ubuntu 21.x+), etc. have moved to using `nftables`.
remediation: On nodes whose OS defaults to nftables, a VPC CNI below v1.12.1 programs iptables-legacy rules the kernel's nft tables do not see. v1.12.1 ships both binaries (ENABLE_NFTABLES=true selects iptables-nft on 1.12.x) and v1.13.1+ picks the mode from kubelet's automatically — land on 1.13.1+ and drop any custom-built nft image.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.name): \(.status.nodeInfo.osImage)"'  # RHEL 8+, Rocky/Alma, Ubuntu 21+ nodes default to nftables and need VPC CNI v1.12.1+

title: Rolling back below v1.12.1 after running it can leave pod deletion failing (#2321)

detection.reason: a rollback hazard: nothing in the current state shows which pods were created under which CNI version

quote: If you created pods with VPC CNI version >= 1.12.1, then downgraded to a version < 1.12.1 and pod deletion is failing
remediation: Plan the rollback of this upgrade as 'roll back to v1.12.1 or newer'. If a downgrade below v1.12.1 is unavoidable, recycle the nodes so no pod created by the newer CNI is deleted by the older one.
